images.title: Try, notice, explain
images.purpose: Recap the three step way to turn examples into a general statement, using pairs of multiples of 5.
images.composition: Three panels in one row joined by two grey arrows, each holding at most three short lines, with generous space around.
exact_structure: Panel 1 (teal #0072B2 border), heading 1 Try, with exactly 3 lines: 10 and 15: HCF 5, then 20 and 35: HCF 5, then 15 and 45: HCF 15.
Panel 2 (amber #E69F00 border), heading 2 Notice, with one line: HCF is a multiple of 5.
Panel 3 (reddish purple #CC79A7 border), heading 3 Explain, with one line: 5 divides both numbers.
Exactly 2 grey #6B7280 arrows: panel 1 to panel 2, panel 2 to panel 3.
rejection: any HCF other than 5 for 10 and 15 or for 20 and 35, or other than 15 for 15 and 45
any of the pairs 4 and 6, 10 and 12, 5 and 7, 11 and 13, 7 and 8, 20 and 21, 3 and 24, or 9 and 10 appearing
more or fewer than 3 panels or 2 arrows
images.takeaway: Try several pairs, notice what stays the same, and explain why before calling it a general statement.
images.description: Three panels: three pairs of multiples of 5 with their HCFs, the pattern that the HCF is a multiple of 5, and the reason that 5 divides both.
images.context: Shown beside the practice on exploring pairs of numbers.
images.teaching_notes: Use the same three panels for each pair type in the practice: fill in Try first, then Notice, then Explain.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of the try, notice, explain routine supports the pattern practice without giving away its answers.
